hangar.meta.v1.Condition.description: Condition is one observed aspect of an object's state, such as "Ready".

observedGeneration.description: The generation this condition was computed from.

reason.description: CamelCase machine-readable cause of the last transition.

status.description: ConditionStatus is the state of a condition.

hangar.meta.v1.ObjectMeta.description: ObjectMeta is the metadata every resource carries. Users set name, project, labels and annotations; everything else is owned by the system. See docs/decisions/apply-semantics.md.

annotations.description: Keys under a *.hangarlab.cloud/ prefix are reserved for the system.

deleteTime.description: Set when deletion was requested and finalizers are still pending.

generation.description: Incremented on every change to spec.

labels.description: Keys under a *.hangarlab.cloud/ prefix are reserved for the system.

name.description: DNS-1123 label, unique within the project (or the platform, for global kinds). An Invitation's is an email instead.

resourceVersion.description: Store revision of the last write to this object.

hangar.meta.v1.OwnerReference.description: OwnerReference points at the object that owns this one. An owner is in the same project, a global object, or, for a global object, one in the project the reference names; when it is deleted, its dependents are garbage collected.

controller.description: The owner is the controller responsible for this object.

project.description: The owner's project, when the owner is project-scoped and this object is global, as a RoleBinding owned by the ServiceToken it names. Empty otherwise.

hangar.network.v1alpha1.EgressRule.description: EgressRule lets out what goes to a peer.

protocol.description: SecurityGroupProtocol is what a rule matches.

hangar.network.v1alpha1.IngressRule.description: IngressRule lets in what comes from a peer.

ports.description: Ports, such as "443", "8000-8080" or "80,443"; empty is every port. Only TCP and UDP take ports.

protocol.description: SecurityGroupProtocol is what a rule matches.

hangar.network.v1alpha1.SecurityGroupPee.description: SecurityGroupPeer is the other end of a rule.

cidr.description:
An IPv4 or IPv6 range, such as "0.0.0.0/0", "10.0.0.0/24" or "::/0". A range matches only addresses of its own family.

Set at most one of cidr, group, network.

group.description:
The members of a group of the same network, "default" included.

Set at most one of cidr, group, network.

network.description:
Names another Network of the project: what reaches a member through that network's NetworkEndpoints, which comes from the network's transit address (docs/decisions/endpoint-services.md). Only ingress rules take it.

Set at most one of cidr, group, network.

egress.description: What a member may send. Empty lets everything out; once one group of an interface has egress rules, the interface sends only what some rule of its groups allows.

ingress.description: What may come into a member.

network.description: Names a network in the group's project; only its interfaces join the group.

hangar.network.v1alpha1.SecurityGroupSta.description: SecurityGroupStatus is the envelope's status. Nothing writes it: a group's rules take effect on the nodes, which report through each Machine's status, not here.

description: SecurityGroup is a set of allow rules for the interfaces on one network that name it, as in AWS: stateful, ingress denied unless a rule allows it, egress open unless the group has egress rules. Every network also has an implicit group "default", which is no object: it lets in its own members. See docs/decisions/networking.md.
title: SecurityGroup
